text:
maria: Ran a subnet-eviction sim in eu-west-1 this morning. ~8 GPU nodes got evicted during the firewall rule apply and none of them fully rejoined the warm pool within 5m. Keystore proxy shows intermittent 503s during the window.
jon: Oof. Was this the planned test? Any overlap with audit-log maintenance?
maria: Yes planned. We toggled the stateful rule set -> default-deny then back. We also rotated a keystore endpoint as part of the test. timing aligned.
infra-bot: [automation] test-run-id=sim-2026-03-22-09:12
infra-bot: nodes_evicted=8 warmpool_rejoin_fail=6 keystore_503_count=42
oliver: 503s from the keystore proxy usually point at per-shard qps limits or the HSM proxy backpressure. Can you drop the keystore proxy logs snippet?
maria: paste: ```
2026-03-22T09:12:34Z keystore-proxy: rpc error: code=14 desc="upstream returned 503"
2026-03-22T09:12:37Z keystore-proxy: throttle=true shard=eu-west-1-3
``` 
oliver: shard-level throttle. Did the firewall change increase connection churn so conntrack table filled and new proxy handshakes retried -> spike?
sre-jen: Also saw a temporary audit-exporter lag during the same window — we had sampling toggled to 0 for config sync. Might have reduced overall observability. auditor-bot flagged missing audit spans.
auditor-bot: ALERT: audit-exporter-gap detected for namespace=vpc-writes window=120s samples_lost=~500
jon: So two issues: (1) keystore proxy shard throttle, (2) conntrack/churn exacerbated by firewall-cycles. Both made nodes fail join. Any region-specific constraints? eu-west1 has tighter NATGW conntrack limits right now.
maria: Correct. eu-west-1 NATGW conntrack already near 80% from recent load. The test pushed it over. Nodes trying to call keystore failed, then join watchers timed out.
oliver: Short-term mitigation: schedule firewall apply in a maintenance window while temporarily increasing keystore shard capacity and bumping conntrack SNAT mapping limit. Also pre-warm the warm-pool by creating 3 transient nodes per AZ before evict.
sre-jen: For canary, we should run the sim against a single AZ with keystore shard boosted and audit logging ON to get full traces. If that succeeds, roll to other AZs.
jon: Cost tradeoff: boosting keystore shards + pre-warm nodes will cost ~€120/hr for the window. We think acceptable for scheduled maintenance vs outage risk.
maria: Ops plan draft:
  - rollback firewall change if observed rejoin fail count >3
  - boost keystore shard pool (autoscale override) 10m before apply
  - increase conntrack limit on natgw via template for the test AZs
  - pre-create 3 warm nodes per AZ 15m before
  - keep audit-exporter sampling at 100% during the window
  - run sim in single AZ canary -> if green, proceed
oliver: Add a fallback of cross-region fallback to eu-central-1 model variant if we see sustained join failures (reduces latency but keeps capacity online).
sre-jen: Also add a post-mortem checklist: collect keystore-proxy logs, conntrack metrics, natgw metrics, kubelet join traces, and full audit spans. Set retention to 7d for this run.
jon: Who wants to own the run? maria: you on-call today, can you lead? maria: I can. I'll open the maintenance ticket and set calendar entry.
maria: Ticket: https://tickets.internal/INFRA-1359 - I'll attach the sim run artifacts and link to rollback playbook.
infra-bot: scheduled_maintenance=INFRA-1359 window=2026-03-23T02:00Z duration=60m owner=maria
oliver: One last ask: make sure the keystore autoscale override includes a cooldown so it doesn't immediately scale down post-apply and create a second blip.
sre-jen: Agreed. I'll add that to the runbook.
jon: Thanks everyone. Quick wins: keep audit sampling on during triage, pre-warm nodes, and bump keystore capacity. We'll reconvene after canary.
maria: noted. Starting checklist now. :thumbsup:
